```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab08", title = "Mock day")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "report() on an ETS fit is used to read:",
  q2 = "accuracy() should be compared:",
  q3 = "A residual ACF spike at the seasonal lag means:",
  q4 = "In two sentences, how would you write a Section C answer (model name, one plot clue, one residual note, the scale)?"
)
```

## What you will do

Recall what Section C of the midterm asks you to read.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Error, trend, and season letters, plus smoothing parameters", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Only the AICc number"),
  answer("The future regressor path"),
  answer("A Prophet holiday list"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("On the same hold-out and the original scale, against a naive baseline", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Using training AICc only"),
  answer("On the log scale even if the question asks for GDP"),
  answer("Only for the model you like"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Seasonality is still missing", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The model is white noise"),
  answer("You should set p equal to that lag"),
  answer("The mean is wrong but the dynamics are fine"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Name the class, cite one feature, one residual comment, state the scale.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
